messages.body_plain:
Hi!

Continuing with this topic, I'm also using a state-space model for solving a dynamic inverse problem. So far it's working well for models ​with simple structures but I'm curious if using this option available in RTMB could accelerate the computation or guarantee the convergence for more complex models written in TMB (as Jeff Eaton also asked). So, is there any option to manually integrate this "ridge" correction to the Laplace approximation in TMB?

Thank you in advance.
Best,

El miércoles, 18 de febrero de 2026 a las 17:28:28 UTC+1, cole.m...@noaa.gov escribió:
> I would support the renaming. I've already experienced this confusion when talking to someone about this feature. It seems likely that adding "but this is not ridge regression" will follow this feature around if not renamed. -Cole
>
> On Tuesday, February 17, 2026 at 10:46:17 AM UTC-8 mollie...@gmail.com wrote:
> > Before this method gains popularity, can it please be renamed "ravine" instead of "ridge". Figure 2 in the slideshow clearly shows a ravine, but my main concern is that "ridge regression" already exists in our field. Would it help if I did a pull request?
> >
> > I'm preparing my teaching material and I don't want any new users to think that ridge regression is done automatically.
> >
> > cheers,
> > Mollie
> >
> > On Tuesday, December 16, 2025 at 3:19:48 PM UTC+1 Kasper Kristensen wrote:
> > > Jeff, so far the method is only available in RTMB.
> > >
> > >
> > > On Tuesday, December 16, 2025 at 12:47:32 AM UTC+1 Jeff Eaton wrote:
> > > > Thanks for sharing these slides — this has been a longstanding intermittent issue for us, with limited traction on addressing.
> > > >
> > > > To confirm, can the ridge correction be tested in ‘normal’ TMB (not RTMB) simply by specifying the argument below?
> > > >
> > > > obj <- MakeADFun(..., ridge.correct=TRUE)​
> > > >
> > > > Thanks,
> > > > Jeff
> > > >
> > > > From: 'Matt Cheng' via TMB Users <tmb-...@googlegroups.com>
> > > > Date: Monday, December 15, 2025 at 11:26 AM

> > > > Cc: TMB Users <tmb-...@googlegroups.com>

> > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > I believe this was partly discussed during the 2024 ICES MGWG?

messages.body_plain:
Sorry that I haven't looked closely at the code, but I do something similar in `package:ecostate`, search `log_prior` argument here <https://github.com/James-Thorson-NOAA/ecostate/blob/main/R/ecostate.R>.

On Fri, Mar 13, 2026 at 3:50 PM Paul vdb <paul.van...@gmail.com> wrote:

> What is the most efficient way to allow a user to pass a custom function to the likelihood?
>
> Here is one way I have done it.
>
> extractValue <- function(x, y){
>   if(!is.null(x)) return(x)
>   return(y)
> }
>
> mycars_bayeslm <- function(sd_prior = NULL, beta_priors = NULL){
>   dprior_sd <- extractValue(sd_prior, function(x){dgamma(1, 1, log = TRUE)})
>   dprior_beta <- extractValue(sd_prior, function(x){sum(dnorm(0, 10, log = TRUE))})
>
>   parinit <- list(beta = c(0,0), sd = 5)
>   negll <- function(pars){
>     getAll(cars, pars)
>     -sum(dnorm(dist, beta[1] + beta[2] * speed, sd, log = TRUE)) - dprior_sd(sd) - dprior_beta(beta)
>   }
>   obj <- MakeADFun(negll, parinit)
>   return(obj)
> }
>
> obj1 <- mycars_bayeslm()
> obj2 <- mycars_bayeslm(sd_prior = function(x){dnorm(x[1], 1, 10, log = TRUE)})
>
> If I am not explicit about returning a scalar, then it does not work, which is minorly annoying.
> obj3 <- mycars_bayeslm(sd_prior = function(x){dnorm(x, 1, 10, log = TRUE)})
>
> Does anyone have a better solution? Any suggestions? Thanks so much.
>

> --
